baslik: Motorcycle Navigation and Route Planner — Motoseyir
aciklama: Distance-first navigation for motorcyclists: shortest route, back roads, multi-stop tours, group riding, intercom and legendary routes. Motoseyir, on the App Store.
jsonld_aciklama: Distance-first navigation app for motorcyclists: shortest route, back roads, multi-stop tours, group riding, intercom and legendary routes.
jsonld_ucretsiz: Unlimited routing and navigation in Türkiye, Europe and the USA, 1 saved tour; Pro’s 3-month and yearly plans include a 7-day free trial outside Türkiye, for new subscribers.
jsonld_pro: Best order for multiple stops, unlimited tours and trails, Back roads and Coast modes, Discover, group creation, intercom and AI CoRider.
hero_alt: A motorcyclist riding a twisty mountain road along the coast in the light of sunset
hero_h1: The only sat nav that counts the kilometres.
hero_lead: Motoseyir works out the route by distance, not by minutes. It compares several alternatives between the same two points and suggests the shortest one. On a multi-stop tour it works out the order of the stops, too.
hero_micro: Routing and navigation are free and unlimited in Türkiye, Europe and the USA; no account needed.
neden_soz:
Other sat navs find the fastest road.
Motoseyir finds the shortest one.
neden_alt: A route calculated for a car always makes the same mistake on a bike: it shaves off minutes and adds kilometres. You filter through traffic, so that difference is real for you — more fuel, more tyre wear. Motoseyir compares the alternatives and suggests the shortest one, even if it takes a few minutes longer.
oz_h2: One app for everything a rider does
oz_lead: Route, tour, ride and riding together — four headings, one app. The screens below are from the app itself.
f1_p: It calculates several alternative routes between the same two points and suggests the one with the shortest distance — even if it takes a little longer.
f1_alt: Screen comparing the shortest-distance route with the alternatives
f2_p: In Back roads mode the route comes from our own server, which also uses the lanes a standard map skips. Ayder to Hemşin comes out at 24.1 km that way; general maps show 49.9 km for the same two points. Coast mode uses the same server to keep the route along the shoreline.
f2_alt: A route drawn in Back roads mode, full of bends and scenery
f3_p: You enter the delivery points in any order and “Best order” rearranges them for the shortest total distance. The example below is from a real ride: the same four stops, 57.1 km in your own order, 46.9 km in the order the app found.
f3_alt_a: Four stops in the rider’s own order, 57.1 km in total
f3_alt_b: The same four stops in the order Motoseyir found, 46.9 km in total
f4_p: Alpine passes like the Stelvio and the Sellaronda are ready and waiting, along with Turkish classics such as Şile–Ağva and the Lycian D400 and seven American ones, Tail of the Dragon and Big Sur included. Open one from the list and it goes straight into your tours with its stops and its route.
f4_alt: The list of ready-made legendary routes
f5_h3: Group ride, Invite to ride and intercom
f5_p: When one person creates a group a single code is generated, everyone joins with that code, and you all see each other on the route. In My Ride Group, “Invite to ride” next to a friend sends your route and a voice link in one tap; they answer with “Ride the same route” or “Riding behind you”.
f5_p2: The intercom also starts without a route. Each friend’s volume is set separately and Bluetooth helmets connect directly. Nothing is recorded — the audio goes only to whoever is in the room at that moment, and the room closes when the ride ends.
f5_alt: Friends’ live positions on the route during a group ride
f6_p: At every stop you take a photo and leave a short note, and both stay under that stop. The photos also show up as cards on the tour map; tap one to open it full screen. The journal stays on your phone; if you choose to share it in Community, at most three photos go with it.
f6_alt: Tour journal: adding a photo and a note to a stop
f7_p: If rain is expected on your route, it warns you in advance for the time you will actually get there. If the weather is dry, nothing appears on screen.
f7_alt: Weather warning along the route in the tour plan
f8_p: Ride recording keeps running with the screen off, and the track is coloured by speed. You can send a finished ride to your group: the track, distance and time stay there for 14 days. For a trail you brought in as GPX it works out the distance, total climb and steepest gradient; as you slide your finger along the profile, the point on the map moves with it.
f8_alt: Trail elevation profile with distance, climb and difficulty figures
f9_p: It lists the coves, campsites and places to eat around your route. You look at the rating and how far it is from your route, then add the one you like as a stop.
f9_alt: The Discover screen: suggestions around your route
d1_p: You see the estimated fuel cost of the route before you set off. It calculates in litres per 100 km where that is the local unit, and in miles per gallon in the US.
d2_p: Turn instructions are spoken by your phone’s voice in the app’s language; with the app in Turkish they come from a recorded human voice-over instead. Distances follow your region — “In 500 feet, turn right” in the US.
d3_p: The tours you share appear in the feed with your username and icon, and others can like and comment on them. Posts are reviewed before they go live. Around 400 metres near your start and finish are trimmed before anything is shared.
d4_p: Turn the phone sideways and the map, cards and buttons switch to a new layout: in navigation the turn and arrival cards sit on the left and the map on the right; My Tours shows two columns.
d5_p: You pick your marker from the grid in Settings: bike, chopper, maxi scooter, touring, arrow or helmet. The three added in the latest update show the rider as well.
fiyat_h2: Free to ride, Pro when you want more
fiyat_lead: No account needed. Routing and navigation are free and unlimited in Türkiye, Europe and the USA, with 1 saved tour. Pro’s 3-month and yearly plans start with a 7-day free trial outside Türkiye, for new subscribers; cancel anytime in your store account.
plan_ucretsiz_notu: On the 3-month and yearly plans, for new subscribers where available.
pu5: Joining a group by invite or code
plan_pro_notu: Current prices vary by region; you see yours on the subscription screen in the App Store.
pp4: Back roads, Coast and Enduro modes
gizlilik_lead: You do not have to give a name, an email address or a phone number to use Motoseyir. What follows is a short summary of the privacy policy; the full policy is inside the app in English, under Settings → Privacy Policy.
g1: You do not need to create an account — we do not ask for your name, email address, phone number or date of birth.
g2: To calculate your route, your location and search queries are passed to map services only; none of them store anything.
g3: Your tours, ride recordings, journal notes and photos stay only on your device — unless you share them in Community.
g4: An irreversible, anonymous identity hash of your device is sent to our server to stop trial and campaign entitlements being abused; that hash does not identify you.
g5: If you turn on group riding, your last location is shared only while the ride is running and is deleted when it ends. Intercom audio is never recorded, only passed to whoever is in the room at that moment.
g6: No ads; no data is shared with any advertising network.
gizlilik_baglanti: Read the privacy summary in English →

oz_aciklama: Every feature of the Motoseyir motorcycle navigation app on one page: shortest route, stop order, back roads, legendary routes, tour journal, group riding.
oz_sayfa_lead: This page grows. When a new feature arrives it goes here first, under the heading it belongs to. There are five groups below: city and courier riding, touring, on the road and after the ride, riding together, and in the mountains and in the car.
oz1_p: A standard sat nav gives you the fastest road for a car. On a bike what wears you out is not minutes but kilometres. Motoseyir compares several alternatives between the same two points and suggests the shortest one, even if it takes a little longer. Turn-by-turn navigation gives you a close-following map, turn instructions, remaining distance and arrival time.
oz2_p: You mark several delivery points in any order and “Best order” rearranges them all for the shortest total distance. The time you will reach each stop is written above the route as well. The two screens below are from a real ride: the same four stops in Istanbul, 57.1 km in the rider’s own order, 46.9 km in the order Motoseyir found. The difference is more than ten kilometres.
oz3_p: You see the estimated amount of fuel for the route on its card before you set off: litres in most places, gallons in the US. Tap the consumption on the card to enter your own; add the fuel price under Settings → Riding and the savings report works out your fuel savings.
oz4_p: Back roads avoids the motorway and uses the valley links and surfaced lanes a standard map skips. In Türkiye and Greece the route is calculated on Motoseyir’s own server; Ayder to Hemşin comes out at 24.1 km that way, while general maps show 49.9 km for the same two points. Coast mode holds the route along the shoreline; it works in Türkiye and in most of Europe’s coastal countries, and where there is no coastline to follow the route is calculated like Back roads. On the Route screen you switch between Shortest and Back roads for free; on the tour screen the mode button at the top left switches between Standard, Back roads and Coast (the last two are Pro).
oz5_p: From Turkey: Şile–Ağva, the Lycian D400, Assos–Kaz Mountains, Nemrut, Sapanca–Maşukiye–Kartepe (11 tours in all). From Europe: Großglockner Hochalpenstraße, Stelvio Pass, Furka–Grimsel–Susten, Sellaronda, Timmelsjoch, Col du Galibier (17 roads in all). From the US: Tail of the Dragon, Cherohala Skyway, Blue Ridge Parkway, Beartooth Highway, Big Sur, Million Dollar Highway (26 roads in all). The Turkish ones are copied into your tours with their stops and route as soon as you open them; for European and US roads a page about the road opens first, and Ride this road builds the route.
oz6_p: In My Tours, the Discover tab of a tour lists the coves and beaches, campsites, places to eat, fuel stops and passes around it. Each row shows the rating and which stop it is near, and you add the one you like as a stop. Tap a place and its location, rating and a short description appear on one screen. The tab is open to everyone; the search is part of Pro.
oz6_alt_b: The detail screen for a place along the route
oz7_p: You build the tour out of stops; when you reach one, that stop is written into the journal by itself and you add a photo and a short note. A stop can hold up to three photos, and the photos show up as cards on the tour map. They are kept even if you start the tour over. The journal stays on your device; if you choose to share it in Community at most three photos go with it, and you pick which ones.
oz8_p: Import a GPX file and the track lands on the Trail tab; a tour from a friend’s code lands on the Tours tab. While the Trail tab is empty it explains what it is for and offers a ready-made example trail for your region. You can also turn one of your own ride recordings into a trail and export it as GPX.
kume3_h2: On the road and after the ride
oz9_p: If rain is expected on your route it warns you in advance, for the time you will actually get there. The Route screen checks four points along the route and shows one warning; in My Tours every stop also gets its own forecast. If there is no rain on the route, no warning appears.
oz10_p: Ride recording keeps running with the screen off and the track is coloured by speed; break time is counted separately and long breaks close a segment by themselves. You start the recording out on the road with the button in navigation and end it with the same button. A finished ride can be sent to your group, turned into a trail, or exported as GPX. For a trail it works out the distance, total climb and steepest gradient, and as you slide your finger along the elevation profile the point on the map moves with it. If the file holds no elevation data, it is calculated from a terrain model.
oz11_p: Turn instructions are spoken by your phone’s voice in the app’s language; with the app in Turkish they come from a recorded human voice-over, re-recorded in the latest update. Distances follow the region you are in: kilometres in most of Europe, miles and feet in the US (“In 500 feet, turn right”), miles and yards in the UK.
oz12_p: Hold the phone in landscape and cards and lists gather on the left while the map takes the rest. In navigation the manoeuvre strip and arrival card sit on the left and the map on the right; My Tours switches to two columns. On the wide mounts that sit above the tank, that layout simply works better.
oz13_p: When one person creates a group a single code is generated (A3K9MZ7P, for example), everyone joins with that code, and you all see each other on the route. Location is shared only while a ride recording or navigation is running, and it is deleted from the server when the ride ends. Joining a group is free; creating one needs Pro. When a member opens a route with Start, the same route goes to the others, who open it on their own screen with one tap.
oz13_p2: The group panel was simplified in the latest update: code on top, people first, settings below. The group button shows when sharing is on, and a stop added to the route is marked on the map.
oz14_p: In My Ride Group, “Invite to ride” next to a person sends your route and a voice link in one tap. Whoever gets it picks “Ride the same route” and opens the same route on their own phone, or “Riding behind you” and joins the audio only. No codes to type, no screens to share.
oz15_p: While a group route is being ridden the intercom asks once; accept and the audio goes only to your group. You can also start it by hand with no route at all. Tapping the intercom pill in navigation mutes your own microphone; the speaker button in the member list mutes one rider in your ear only, while the rest of the group still hears them. Pair your helmet or headset over Bluetooth and the audio comes through it. Audio is never recorded on our server, only passed to whoever is in the room at that moment; the room closes when navigation ends or when you close it yourself.
oz16_h3: Ride recordings in the group, and the Community feed
oz16_p: Send a finished ride to your group and the track, distance and time stay there for 14 days; around 400 metres near the start and the end are never sent. You can take a recording you sent back whenever you like. The Community feed, on the other hand, is public to riders in your region: a tour you share appears with its name, stops, distance, time and your note, and others can like and comment on it. A new member’s first post is reviewed before it goes live and later ones are published straight away; you can filter the feed by country, and you can remove a post, a comment or your membership whenever you want.
kume5_h2: In the mountains, on the road and in the car
oz17_p: 1,638 passes in 36 countries, each with its altitude and location and most with a photo; where the closing months are known they’re shown, and dirt roads are marked as dirt. In My Tours → Legendary → Mountain passes you filter by region and sort by popularity, distance from you or altitude, then choose Add to tour or Go here.
oz18_h3: Pick a direction and a time, the tour is ready
oz18_p: Turn the dial to the direction you want (or choose Any direction) and pick a length of 30–300 km or a number of hours; the curviness levels are Relaxed, Twisty and Very twisty. You can leave out motorways, tolls and dirt roads separately. Each time you get three tours, and Another one brings new ones, up to nine options. Anyone can generate a tour and see it on the map; building a twisty or motorway-free one is part of Pro.
oz19_h3: The next turn on the Lock Screen
oz19_p: The next turn shows on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island, so you don’t have to open the phone. You can turn it off under Settings → Riding → Next turn on the Lock Screen; it’s on by default. iPhone only.
oz20_h3: Speed cameras, speed limit and lanes
oz20_p: It warns you on screen 500 m or 20 seconds before each of the 726 speed cameras in Türkiye, and you can turn that off under Settings → Riding. Where the limit is known, a speed-limit sign stays on screen. Lane arrows appear as you approach junctions that have lane data on the map, and on the dashboard of compatible cars.
oz21_h3: Your route on the car screen
oz21_p: Map, turns and distance remaining are on CarPlay. Skip a stop, record the ride, open the intercom or search an address from the Destinations list; while navigating you can search along the route for Fuel, Coffee, Food, Groceries, Pharmacy, Rest area and Motorcycle repair. The marker you picked and your group friends show on the map, and the map also sits in CarPlay Dashboard.
oz22_h3: A riding partner in your helmet
oz22_p: Press the button and ask: it adds stops, finds places along the route, changes the route, and tells you the weather and your fuel range. Pro renews 10 minutes of talk time every 30 days, and there are minute packs that never expire. The details are on the AI CoRider page.
oz23_p: When a ride ends you see moving time, real breaks, sharp bends and climbing. Watch in 3D replays it in Apple’s helicopter view at 1, 5, 20 or 60 times speed, and you can save it as a vertical video of 15, 30 or 60 seconds. The trip map video shows a tour on a clean map. There are also 22 badges, GPX export and an Instagram Story card.
oz24_p: On the map you are a Supersport, Chopper, Maxi scooter, Touring, Arrow or Helmet. You pick it under Settings → Map → Navigation marker, and CarPlay shows the same one. The first four are 3D with a rider on board and lean into bends.
ny_baslik: How to Use Motoseyir Motorcycle Navigation, Step by Step
ny_aciklama: How to plan a motorcycle route in Motoseyir: building a route, multi-stop tours, ride recording, the tour journal, group riding, the intercom and subscriptions.
ny_h1: How to use Motoseyir, start to finish
ny_lead: This page is the long version of Settings → “How it works” inside the app: same topics, same order. Tap a heading to open it, tap again to close.
hb1: On the Start tab, type in the field at the top and pick a suggestion → the destination is added and the route is drawn.
hb2: Start on the card at the bottom → navigation opens and the strip at the top shows the next manoeuvre.
hb3: Tap Start recording on the Record tab, or choose Record ride in the ⋯ menu during navigation → the ride recording starts; the record button that shows while it runs ends it.
hb4: On the My Tours tab, type a name and tap Create → you start building your multi-stop tour.
hb5: Settings → Redeem an App Store offer code: if you have an App Store offer code (a gift from us, for example), redeem it here.
rota1: Type in the field at the top and pick a suggestion → the destination is added; anything after the second one becomes a multi-stop route.
rota2: Tap a place name on the map → its card opens, and you add it from the chip inside the card.
rota3: Long-press an empty spot on the map → it asks whether to make that point a destination or a stop.
rota4: The sign button on the right → switches between Shortest (fewest kilometres) and Back roads (side roads instead of motorways and toll roads).
rota5: Best order on a multi-stop route → the stops are arranged for the shortest total riding distance.
rota6: While navigating, the frame button on the right → the rest of the route fits on screen; a second tap brings the camera back to the bike.
tur1: In My Tours, type a name and tap Create → an empty tour opens; you add stops by searching or by long-pressing the map.
tur2: The mode button at the top left → switches between Standard, Back roads and Coast (the last two are Pro).
tur3: From GPX or With a code → a track from a file lands on the Trail tab, a tour from a friend’s code on the Tours tab.
tur4: Tap a route on the Legendary tab → the ready-made route is copied into your own tours.
tur5: The Discover tab of a tour → lists the coves, campsites, places to eat, fuel stops and passes around it (the search is Pro).
tur6: Start the tour → the stops are handed to navigation in order, and you pick up where you left off.
kayit1: Start recording on the Record tab → the track, speed and elevation are collected; recording continues with the screen off.
kayit2: Record ride in the ⋯ menu during navigation → starts the same recording out on the road; while it runs, a second tap on the record button ends it.
kayit3: Pause and Resume → the recording stops and picks up where it left off; End segment closes that leg and starts a new one (long breaks close it by themselves).
kayit4: Send the recording to the group → from the card that appears when the ride ends, or from the ride card; your group sees your track, distance and time.
kayit5: Finish and save → you get a summary of distance, time, speed and elevation, and the ride joins the My Rides list.
kayit6: Save this ride as a trail and Export as GPX on the ride card → the track becomes a tour, or a file you can share.
gunluk1: When you reach a stop → that stop is written into the Journal tab by itself.
gunluk2: Add photo on the stop row → you shoot one with the camera or pick one from the gallery.
gunluk3: Add note → you write your own note for that stop.
gunluk4: Photos that reach the journal show up as mini cards on the tour map → tap one to open it full screen.
gunluk5: Photos and notes are kept even if you start the tour over.
grup1: The group button on the Start tab → Create a group (Pro), or type a friend’s code and Join the group (free).
grup2: Share the code → whoever opens the link joins the same group.
grup3: The Show my location switch → your location is shared only while a ride recording or navigation is running, and it is deleted from the server when the ride ends.
grup4: Open under Active routes → the route your friend is riding opens on your phone too.
grup5: Shared recordings → the rides your group has sent; Add to my tours makes one of them your own tour.
grup6: Remove recording from the group takes back one you sent; recordings are deleted by themselves after 14 days.
int1: While a group route is being ridden the intercom asks once → accept and the audio goes only to your group, and is never recorded.
int2: Start the intercom without a route → you join your group’s voice room even when there is no route at all.
int3: The intercom pill in navigation → one tap mutes your own microphone, another turns it back on.
int4: The speaker button in the member list → mutes that rider in your ear only; the rest of the group still hears them.
int5: Pair your helmet or headset over Bluetooth → the audio comes through it and you talk without touching the phone.
top1: Choose a username on the Community tab → you join without an email or a password.
top2: The pencil at the top right → you share the tours you created yourself, plus your ride recordings.
top3: Ready-made routes and tours received from someone else cannot be shared → the picker states the reason under the row.
top4: Your first post goes through moderator approval → while it waits it shows with an Awaiting approval badge.
top5: The country filter → only tours from the countries you pick stay in the feed.
top6: The three-dot menu on a card → you report the post or block the user.
ayar1: Appearance → colour theme and app language.
ayar2: Map → layer (standard or satellite), map theme, rain radar and the navigation marker: Supersport, Chopper, Maxi scooter, Touring, Arrow, Helmet.
ayar3: Riding → voice guidance (including the short mode), fuel consumption and price, tank range, speed camera alerts, next turn on the Lock Screen, the battery saver screen; the savings report is worked out from the fuel values.
ayar4: Redeem an App Store offer code → Apple’s own code screen opens; enter the code and Pro turns on right away.
ayar5: Write to us from the Support row → you see the reply in the same place; the Instagram row announces new features.
ayar6: Turn the phone to landscape → cards and lists gather on the left and the map takes the rest; navigation works the same way.
abo1: 3-month and yearly plans → new subscribers get a 7-day free trial; cancel at least 24 hours before it ends and you won't be charged.
abo2: Invited to a group ride → you can join free with the invite link.
abo3: Motoseyir Pro → unlimited tours and trails, tour modes, Discover, creating groups, CarPlay and AI CoRider.
abo4: AI CoRider → 10 minutes a month with Pro, 5 minutes in the trial; minute packs add more.
abo5: Settings → Restore purchases: you get your subscription back on a new phone.
ny_dip: Something not covered here? Write to us inside the app from Settings → “Something wrong, or an idea?”; the reply comes back in the same place.
